governance.residuals_note: DETERMINATION NOT-YET, fully scored; promoted as the NYISO keeper over nyiso-68 on rule 1 (most structurally faithful: two real reserve mechanisms nyiso-68 lacked, zero new tunable) — both runs are NOT-YET. Scorecard vs nyiso-68 (calibration_verdict RT-basis): C1 PASS unchanged; C2/C4 PASS; C5a CO2 2025 +8.5% CAVEAT (reserve-inert). C3 WINS (2023): C3b shape NRMSE 0.215->0.198 CLOSES (C3b now PASS all years); C3a mean +17.8%->+15.9% and C3c tail 3.10x->2.20x both IMPROVE (still just over band); 2024/2025 hold every C3 criterion (C3a 2024 +0.9%->-0.7%, 2025 +2.8%->+1.6%). LOYO holds — the mechanism moves every year toward actual with no cross-fold regression. KNOWN REGRESSION (recorded, not hidden): C7 diurnal shape for ST_GAS 2023 flips PASS->FAIL (off-peak CV ratio 0.548->0.483, threshold 0.5) — the added reserve supply lets ST_GAS provide less reserve, flattening its off-peak dispatch just below the gate; marginal (0.483 vs 0.5), single-class, confined to the already-NOT-YET 2023 (2024/2025 ST_GAS C7 PASS 0.703/0.641). Owner-authorized promotion 2026-07-22 with this trade in view. Remaining root cause of the 2023 misses: the C3a MEAN-level gap (+15.9%) is NOT reserve-driven (the full reserve over-spike is only ~1.6% of the system mean), a broad 2023 energy-price LEVEL issue (offer surface / gas basis / import pricing) — a separate lever, and the likely lever for the ST_GAS off-peak shape as well. No residual tune taken.

_open_items: (1) LOAD-BEARING ROOT CAUSE — the 2023 C3a MEAN-level gap (+15.9%) is NOT reserve-driven (lever 3 fully absorbed the reserve over-spike, which was only ~1.6% of the system mean). It is a broad 2023 energy-price LEVEL residual (candidate levers: CC/ST offer surface, Transco/Iroquois gas basis, neighbor import pricing) — a separate workstream, NOT a residual tune (rule 22). This lever is also the most likely fix for the C7 ST_GAS 2023 off-peak shape (see (3)). (2) Lever 3 (hydro + SCR/EDRP 30-min reserve-supply eligibility) is DONE and is the reason C3b 2023 closed and C3c/C3a improved; the nyiso-68 _open_items (1) reserve-supply fix is CLOSED. Remaining East-side piece: add Blenheim-Gilboa PS (~1160 MW, prime-mover PS, excluded from build_hydro_fleet) to the dispatch fleet for East-10min reserve — secondary to the SENY-30min DR lever already landed. (3) KNOWN C7 REGRESSION: ST_GAS 2023 off-peak CV ratio 0.483 < 0.5 (nyiso-68 passed at 0.548). The reserve reshuffle flattens ST_GAS off-peak dispatch. Marginal and confined to 2023; owner-authorized as an accepted trade for the C3b close. Expected to resolve with the (1) energy-price-level lever, which governs ST_GAS off-peak dispatch shape. (4) offer_curve_by_group re-tune remains deliberately NOT taken (rule 22).

entries.name: nyiso_scr_edrp
entries.note: NYISO SCR/EDRP emergency demand response as endogenous per-zone price-responsive supply blocks. Capacity = Gold-Book-registered SCR+EDRP MW per model zone (2023/24/25 summer 1.23/1.29/1.49 GW, scripts/data/build_nyiso_scr_edrp.py, byte-identical to the transcribed enrollment CSV). Strike = the published NYISO EDRP $500/MWh compensation floor (Market Services Tariff §5.12) — a market-design constant, NOT a residual. Clears the energy balance only when the zone LBMP exceeds the strike (endogenous scarcity trigger, never pinned to observed event dates; rule 13/17). ZERO fitted values; re-derives for a forward year from the next Gold Book (rule 23). Excluded from generation-mix scoring (avoided load, not generation).

entries.name: nyiso_hydro_reserve_eligible
